### 1. Apportionment Formula
* **Fact:** Wisconsin uses a **single sales factor** (100% sales factor) apportionment formula for multistate business income. The apportionment fraction consists of Wisconsin sales in the numerator and total sales everywhere in the denominator.
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official Sources:**
  * Wis. Stat. § 71.25(6): https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/statutes/statutes/71/iv/25
  * Wis. Admin. Code § Tax 2.39: https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/code/admin_code/tax/2
  * Wisconsin Department of Revenue, *Instructions for Schedule A-01*: https://www.revenue.wi.gov/TaxForms2024/2024-ScheduleA-01-Inst.pdf

---

### 2. Sourcing of Receipts from Services and Intangibles
* **Fact:** Wisconsin uses **market-based sourcing** for both services and intangibles:
  * **Services:** Sourced to Wisconsin if the purchaser of the service receives the benefit of the service in Wisconsin. If the purchaser receives the benefit in more than one state, gross receipts are divided among those states in proportion to the benefit received in each state.
  * **Use/License of Intangible Property:** Gross royalties and receipts from licensing/use are sourced to Wisconsin if the purchaser or licensee uses the intangible property in the operation of a trade or business at a location in Wisconsin or for personal use in Wisconsin. If used in multiple states, receipts are divided in proportion to use.
  * **Sale of Intangible Property:** Gross receipts from sales of intangible property are sourced to Wisconsin if the purchaser uses the property within Wisconsin.
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official Sources:**
  * Wis. Stat. § 71.25(9)(df), (dh), (dj): https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/statutes/statutes/71/iv/25
  * Wis. Admin. Code § Tax 2.39(6): https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/code/admin_code/tax/2
  * Wisconsin Department of Revenue, *Instructions for Schedule A-01*: https://www.revenue.wi.gov/TaxForms2024/2024-ScheduleA-01-Inst.pdf

---

### 3. Specialized Industry Apportionment Formulas
* **Fact:** Specific statutory provisions and administrative rules establish specialized apportionment formulas (or single-factor proxies) for the following industries:
  * **Interstate Financial Institutions** (Receipts factor under Wis. Admin. Code § Tax 2.49)
  * **Interstate Motor Carriers** (Wis. Admin. Code § Tax 2.47)
  * **Interstate Telecommunications Companies** (Wis. Admin. Code § Tax 2.502)
  * **Insurance Companies** (Premiums factor under Wis. Stat. § 71.45(3))
  * **Interstate Broker-Dealers, Investment Advisers, Investment Companies, and Underwriters** (Wis. Admin. Code § Tax 2.495)
  * **Interstate Air Carriers** (Wis. Admin. Code § Tax 2.46)
  * **Broadcasters** (Wis. Stat. § 71.25(9)(g) and Wis. Admin. Code § Tax 2.39)
  * **Interstate Railroads and Car Line Companies** (Wis. Admin. Code § Tax 2.475)
  * **Interstate Pipeline Companies** (Wis. Admin. Code § Tax 2.48)
  * **Interstate Air Freight Forwarders Affiliated with a Direct Air Carrier** (Wis. Admin. Code § Tax 2.465)
  * **Interstate Public Utilities** (Wis. Admin. Code § Tax 2.50)
  * **Interstate Professional Sports Clubs** (Wis. Admin. Code § Tax 2.505)
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official Sources:**
  * Wis. Stat. § 71.25(10)(c): https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/statutes/statutes/71/iv/25
  * Wis. Admin. Code Chapter Tax 2: https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/code/admin_code/tax/2
  * Wisconsin Department of Revenue, *Instructions for Schedule A-01*: https://www.revenue.wi.gov/TaxForms2024/2024-ScheduleA-01-Inst.pdf

---

### 4. Forms and Schedules Used to Compute Apportionment
* **Fact:** Apportionment is reported and computed on the following dedicated schedules filed with the applicable Wisconsin base return (Form 4, 5S, 3, 6, 1NPR, 2, or 4T):
  * **Standard / Nonspecialized Industries:** **Schedule A-01** (*Wisconsin Single Sales Factor Apportionment Data for Nonspecialized Industries*).
  * **Specialized Industry Schedules:**
    * **Schedule A-02:** Interstate Financial Institutions
    * **Schedule A-03:** Interstate Motor Carriers
    * **Schedule A-04:** Interstate Telecommunications Companies
    * **Schedule A-05:** Insurance Companies (Premiums Factor)
    * **Schedule A-06:** Interstate Broker-Dealers, Investment Advisers, Investment Companies, and Underwriters
    * **Schedule A-07:** Interstate Air Carriers
    * **Schedule A-08:** Broadcasters
    * **Schedule A-09:** Interstate Railroads
    * **Schedule A-10:** Interstate Pipeline Companies
    * **Schedule A-11:** Interstate Air Freight Forwarders Affiliated with a Direct Air Carrier
  * *Related schedule:* **Form N** (*Wisconsin Nonapportionable, Separately Accounted, and Separately Apportioned Income*) is used to allocate nonapportionable income.
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official Sources:**
  * Wisconsin Department of Revenue, *Schedule A-01*: https://www.revenue.wi.gov/TaxForms2025/2025-ScheduleA-01.pdf
  * Wisconsin Department of Revenue, *2025 Form 4 Instructions*: https://www.revenue.wi.gov/TaxForms2025/2025-Form4-Inst.pdf
  * Wisconsin Department of Revenue, *Instructions for Schedule A-01*: https://www.revenue.wi.gov/TaxForms2024/2024-ScheduleA-01-Inst.pdf

### 1. Corporate Income / Franchise Tax Nexus & Economic Nexus Thresholds

* **Nexus Standards:**
  * A corporation is subject to Wisconsin corporate income or franchise tax if it is incorporated under Wisconsin law, licensed to transact business in the state, or "doing business in this state".
  * Under Wisconsin law, nexus-creating activities include maintaining a business office or location; owning real estate or tangible personal property (including consignment inventory); holding loans secured by Wisconsin real estate or personal property; and owning an interest in a partnership or LLC doing business in Wisconsin.
* **Economic Nexus Provisions:**
  * Under Wis. Stat. § 71.22(1r) and Wis. Admin. Code § Tax 2.82(4)(b), economic nexus activities (not requiring physical presence) include:
    * Issuing credit cards, debit cards, or travel and entertainment cards to Wisconsin customers.
    * Regularly selling products or services of any kind to customers in Wisconsin that receive them in Wisconsin (unless protected by P.L. 86-272).
    * Regularly soliciting business from potential Wisconsin customers (unless protected by P.L. 86-272).
    * Regularly performing services outside Wisconsin for which the benefits are received in Wisconsin.
    * Regularly engaging in transactions with Wisconsin customers involving intangible property that result in receipts flowing to the taxpayer from within Wisconsin.
* **Bright-Line / Factor-Based Thresholds:**
  * **Factor-Based Dollar Thresholds:** **Not found.** Wisconsin does not have a bright-line dollar/sales-factor economic nexus threshold (e.g., $500,000) for corporate income or franchise tax.
  * **Activity Bright-Line Threshold:** Under Wis. Admin. Code § Tax 2.82(2)(bm), "regular" and "regularly" are defined as **15 or more days of activity** in the state (calculated as 15 person-days: e.g., one person for 15 days, 15 persons for one day, or any combination totaling 15 person-days).
  * *(Note: Wisconsin imposes an Economic Development Surcharge once nexus is established if gross receipts from all activities are $4,000,000 or more).*
* **Applicability:** Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official Sources:**
  * Wis. Stat. § 71.22(1r): https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/statutes/statutes/71/iv/22
  * Wis. Admin. Code § Tax 2.82: https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/code/admin_code/tax/2/82
  * Wisconsin DOR Apportionment and Nexus: https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/FAQS/ise-nexus.aspx
  * Wisconsin DOR Form 4 Instructions (2025): https://www.revenue.wi.gov/TaxForms2025/2025-Form4-Instructions.pdf

---

### 2. Remote Seller Economic Nexus Threshold (Sales and Use Tax)

* **Threshold Amount:** Gross sales into Wisconsin exceeding **$100,000**.
* **Transaction Count:** **None.** Wisconsin eliminated the previous 200-transaction threshold effective February 20, 2021 (2021 Wis. Act 1).
* **Included Sales:** Gross sales include all sales into Wisconsin—taxable sales, exempt sales, and sales for resale.
* **Measurement Period:** The **previous or current calendar year**.
* **Applicability:** Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official Sources:**
  * Wisconsin DOR Remote Sellers Guidance: https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/TaxPro/news-2018-180705a.aspx
  * Wisconsin DOR Remote Sellers Common Questions: https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/FAQS/remote-sellers.aspx
  * Wis. Stat. § 77.51(13gm): https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/statutes/statutes/77/iii/51/13gm

---

### 3. Wisconsin Position on Public Law 86-272 Protection

* **Stated Position:**
  * Wisconsin adheres to P.L. 86-272 (15 U.S.C. §§ 381–384), providing immunity from Wisconsin corporate income or franchise tax measured by net income if the out-of-state business’s only activity in Wisconsin is the solicitation of orders for sales of tangible personal property, provided the orders are sent outside Wisconsin for approval or rejection and filled by shipment or delivery from a point outside the state.
  * **Limitation to Tangible Personal Property:** P.L. 86-272 applies strictly to sellers of tangible personal property; it does not protect businesses selling services, real property, or intangibles (e.g., Software as a Service or travel services).
  * **Unprotected Activities:** Immunity is forfeited if the entity engages in non-solicitation activities in Wisconsin, including approving orders, providing maintenance/repairs, collecting accounts, performing engineering/consulting, storing goods in a warehouse, or exceeding 15 person-days of non-protected regular activities.
* **Adoption of MTC Revised Internet Guidance:** **Not found.** The Wisconsin Department of Revenue has not published administrative rules or official guidance formally adopting the Multistate Tax Commission’s (MTC) revised August 2021 statement on internet activities.
* **Applicability:** Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official Sources:**
  * Wis. Admin. Code § Tax 2.82(3)(b): https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/code/admin_code/tax/2/82
  * Wisconsin DOR Apportionment and Nexus: https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/FAQS/ise-nexus.aspx
  * Wisconsin Tax Bulletin No. 230 (July 2025) / No. 233 (April 2026): https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/TaxPro/news-wtb.aspx

### 1. Individual Income Tax Rates and Brackets

Wisconsin levies an individual income tax with four graduated brackets: **3.50%**, **4.40%**, **5.30%**, and **7.65%**. The bracket thresholds changed between tax years 2025 and 2026 due to annual statutory indexing for inflation.

#### Tax Year 2025 Brackets
* **Single / Head of Household / Estates and Trusts:**
  * $0 to $14,680: 3.50%
  * $14,680 to $50,480: $513.80 + 4.40% of amount over $14,680
  * $50,480 to $323,290: $2,089.00 + 5.30% of amount over $50,480
  * Over $323,290: $16,547.93 + 7.65% of amount over $323,290
* **Married Filing Jointly:**
  * $0 to $19,580: 3.50%
  * $19,580 to $67,300: $685.30 + 4.40% of amount over $19,580
  * $67,300 to $431,060: $2,784.98 + 5.30% of amount over $67,300
  * Over $431,060: $22,064.26 + 7.65% of amount over $431,060
* **Married Filing Separately:**
  * $0 to $9,790: 3.50%
  * $9,790 to $33,650: $342.65 + 4.40% of amount over $9,790
  * $33,650 to $215,530: $1,392.49 + 5.30% of amount over $33,650
  * Over $215,530: $11,032.13 + 7.65% of amount over $215,530

#### Tax Year 2026 Brackets
* **Single / Head of Household / Estates and Trusts:**
  * $0 to $15,110: 3.50%
  * $15,110 to $51,950: $528.85 + 4.40% of amount over $15,110
  * $51,950 to $332,720: $2,149.81 + 5.30% of amount over $51,950
  * Over $332,720: 7.65% of amount over $332,720
* **Married Filing Jointly:**
  * $0 to $20,150: 3.50%
  * $20,150 to $69,260: $705.25 + 4.40% of amount over $20,150
  * $69,260 to $443,630: $2,866.09 + 5.30% of amount over $69,260
  * Over $443,630: $22,707.70 + 7.65% of amount over $443,630
* **Married Filing Separately:**
  * $0 to $10,080: 3.50%
  * $10,080 to $34,630: $352.80 + 4.40% of amount over $10,080
  * $34,630 to $221,820: $1,433.00 + 5.30% of amount over $34,630
  * Over $221,820: $11,354.07 + 7.65% of amount over $221,820

* **Official Sources:** 
  * Wisconsin DOR Tax Rates FAQ: https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/FAQS/ise-taxrates.aspx
  * DOR Publication 106 (*Wisconsin Tax Information for Retirees*): https://www.revenue.wi.gov/DORPublications/pb106.pdf
  * DOR 2026 Form 1-ES Instructions (*Estimated Income Tax for Individuals, Estates, and Trusts*): https://www.revenue.wi.gov/TaxForms2026/2026-Form1-ES-inst.pdf

---

### 2. Corporate Income / Franchise Tax and Minimum Tax

* **Rate:** **7.9%** flat rate on apportioned net taxable income. Imposed as a franchise tax (domestic and foreign corporations doing business in Wisconsin) or an income tax (foreign corporations not subject to the franchise tax with income from Wisconsin sources/property).
* **Minimum Tax:** **None**. Wisconsin does not levy an alternative minimum tax or a fixed-dollar minimum tax on corporate franchise/income tax filers.
* **Applicability:** Applies to both **tax year 2025** and **tax year 2026** (no rate change).
* **Official Sources:**
  * DOR Corporation Franchise or Income Tax General Information: https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/FAQS/ise-corptax.aspx
  * DOR Form 4 Instructions (*Non-Combined Corporate Franchise or Income Tax Return*): https://www.revenue.wi.gov/TaxForms2025/2025-Form4-inst.pdf

---

### 3. State Sales and Use Tax & Local Additions

* **State Rate:** **5.0%** sales tax and **5.0%** use tax.
* **Local Taxes:** Local jurisdictions do add rates:
  * **County Tax:** **0.5%** in participating counties (70 of Wisconsin's 72 counties impose this tax; Manitowoc County effective January 1, 2025; Racine County effective April 1, 2025). **Milwaukee County** imposes a **0.9%** rate.
  * **City Tax:** The **City of Milwaukee** imposes a **2.0%** local sales and use tax (bringing the combined total rate in the City of Milwaukee to **7.9%**: 5.0% state + 0.9% county + 2.0% city).
  * **Special District Taxes:** Certain jurisdictions impose a Premier Resort Area Tax (**0.5%** or **1.25%**) or Local Exposition Taxes (e.g., room, food and beverage, and rental car taxes in the exposition district).
* **Applicability:** Applies to both **tax year 2025** and **tax year 2026**.
* **Official Sources:**
  * DOR Tax Rates FAQ: https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/FAQS/ise-taxrates.aspx
  * DOR Sales and Use Tax Overview: https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/SalesTax/home.aspx
  * DOR County and City Sales and Use Taxes: https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/FAQS/ise-countytax.aspx

---

### 4. Gross Receipts, Franchise, Margin, or Other Notable Business Taxes

* **Economic Development Surcharge:**
  * **Imposition:** Imposed under Wis. Stat. § 77.93 on corporations, insurance companies, exempt organizations, and tax-option (S) corporations that are engaged in business in Wisconsin and have **$4,000,000 or more** of gross receipts from all activities.
  * **Rates:**
    * *Regular C Corporations, Insurance Companies, and Taxable Exempt Organizations:* The greater of **$25** or **3.0%** of gross Wisconsin tax liability, capped at a maximum of **$9,800**.
    * *Tax-Option (S) Corporations:* The greater of **$25** or **0.2%** of Wisconsin net income, capped at a maximum of **$9,800**.
  * **Applicability:** Applies to both **tax year 2025** and **tax year 2026**.
* **Pass-Through Entity-Level Tax (PTE Tax Election):**
  * Partnerships and S corporations may elect to pay tax at the entity level at a flat rate of **7.9%** of Wisconsin net income under Wis. Stat. §§ 71.21(6)(a) and 71.365(4m)(a). Applies to both **tax year 2025** and **tax year 2026**.
* **Official Sources:**
  * DOR Economic Development Surcharge FAQ: https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/FAQS/ise-surchg.aspx
  * DOR Publication 400 (*Wisconsin's Economic Development Surcharge*): https://www.revenue.wi.gov/DORPublications/pb400.pdf
  * DOR Pass-Through Entity-Level Tax Information: https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/FAQS/ise-pass-through-entity-tax.aspx

notes:
### 1. Individual Return Due Dates and Extension Rules
* **Due Date (Calendar-Year Filers):** April 15 following the close of the tax year (e.g., April 15, 2026, for tax year 2025; April 15, 2027, for tax year 2026). If April 15 falls on a weekend or legal holiday, the return is due the next business day.
* **Extension Rules:** 
  * A federal extension (Form 4868) automatically grants a 6-month Wisconsin extension to October 15, provided a copy of the federal extension request is attached to the Wisconsin return when filed.
  * A Wisconsin-only 6-month extension can be obtained without a federal extension by attaching a statement to the Wisconsin return indicating election of the federal extension provision or attaching a copy of federal Form 4868 with only the name and address areas completed.
  * An extension to file does **not** extend the time to pay. Unpaid tax incurs interest at 1% per month (12% per year) during the extension period. 
* **Official URLs:** 
  * https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/FAQS/ise-extensn.aspx
  * https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/FAQS/ise-taxfile.aspx
  * https://www.revenue.wi.gov/DORPublications/pb401.pdf

---

### 2. Corporate and Pass-Through Return Due Dates and Extension Rules
* **C Corporations (Form 4):**
  * **Due Date:** 15th day of the 4th month following the close of the taxable year (April 15 for calendar-year filers).
  * **Extensions:** Wisconsin law provides an automatic extension of 7 months, or until the original due date of the corresponding federal return, whichever is later. A federal extension (Form 7004) extends the Wisconsin due date to 30 days after the federal extended due date.
* **S Corporations / Tax-Option Corporations (Form 5S):**
  * **Due Date:** 15th day of the 3rd month following the close of the taxable year (March 15 for calendar-year filers).
  * **Extensions:** Wisconsin provides an automatic 7-month extension (checked on Item B of Form 5S). A federal extension automatically extends the Wisconsin return due date to 30 days after the federal extended due date.
* **Partnerships (Form 3):**
  * **Due Date:** 15th day of the 3rd month following the close of the taxable year (March 15 for calendar-year filers).
  * **Extensions:** Wisconsin provides a state extension of up to 6 months (checked on Box B of Form 3). A federal extension automatically extends the Wisconsin return to the federal extended due date.
* *Applicability:* Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026.
* **Official URLs:** 
  * https://www.revenue.wi.gov/DORPublications/pb401.pdf
  * https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/FAQS/ise-s-general.aspx
  * https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/FAQS/ise-p-general.aspx

---

### 3. Elective Pass-Through Entity Tax (PTET)
* **Existence:** Yes; authorized under Wis. Stat. § 71.21(6)(a) for partnerships and Wis. Stat. § 71.365(4m)(a) for tax-option (S) corporations.
* **Tax Rate:** 7.9% flat rate on net income reportable to Wisconsin.
* **How to Elect:**
  * **Partnerships:** Check Box I in the return information section of Form 3 (and file Schedule 3-ET). Requires consent from partners holding more than 50% of the capital and profits of the partnership on the date of the election.
  * **S Corporations:** Check Box 7 in Part A of Form 5S (and file Schedule 5S-ET). Requires consent from shareholders holding more than 50% of the shares on the date of the election.
* **When to Elect:** Must be made annually on or before the extended due date of the entity's return (Form 3 or Form 5S) and is made on the date the return is filed.
* *Applicability:* Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026.
* **Official URLs:**
  * https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/FAQS/ise-p-general.aspx
  * https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/FAQS/ise-s-general.aspx
  * https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/FAQS/ise-s-taxcomp.aspx

---

### 4. Composite or Group Nonresident Returns
* **Availability:** Pass-through entities may file composite returns on behalf of qualifying nonresident individual partners or shareholders who have no other Wisconsin source income:
  * **Form 1CNP:** For nonresident partners of a partnership.
  * **Form 1CNS:** For nonresident shareholders of an S corporation.
* **Due Date & Extensions:** Due April 15 following the close of the taxable year. An extension allowed by the IRS for the entity's return automatically extends the due date of Form 1CNS/1CNP to 30 days after the federal extended due date.
* *Applicability:* Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026.
* **Official URLs:**
  * https://www.revenue.wi.gov/DORForms/2025-Form1CNS-inst.pdf
  * https://www.revenue.wi.gov/DORForms/2025-Form1CNP-inst.pdf
  * https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/FAQS/ise-compq.aspx

---

### 5. Estimated Tax Payments and Nonresident Withholding for Pass-Throughs
* **Nonresident Withholding Requirement (Form PW-1):**
  * Pass-through entities must withhold Wisconsin income tax on Wisconsin income allocable to nonresident owners unless exempt.
  * **Exemptions:** Entities that make the elective PTET election under Wis. Stat. § 71.21(6)(a) or § 71.365(4m)(a) are exempt from pass-through withholding (provided no withholding is reported to owners on Schedules 3K-1/5K-1); nonresidents whose allocable Wisconsin income is under $2,000 are also exempt.
  * **Withholding Return Filing:** Form PW-1 is filed annually by the 15th day of the 3rd month following year-end (March 15 for calendar-year filers), with an automatic 7-month extension available.
* **Estimated Payments:**
  * **Pass-Through Withholding Estimated Payments:** Due quarterly on the 15th day of the 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th months of the taxable year (March 15, June 15, September 15, and December 15 for calendar-year filers). Must be submitted electronically via *My Tax Account* (or via Form PW-ES voucher if an electronic payment waiver is approved).
  * **PTET Estimated Tax:** Electing pass-through entities must make quarterly estimated entity-level income tax payments on the 15th day of the 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th months of the taxable year and are subject to statutory underpayment interest if underpaid.
* *Applicability:* Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026.
* **Official URLs:**
  * https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/TaxPro/news-2025-Pass-Through-Withholding-Fact-Sheet.aspx
  * https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/FAQS/ise-pass-through.aspx
  * https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/HTML/pass-through-entity-withholding.aspx

---

### 6. Main Return Forms
* **Individuals:**
  * **Form 1:** Wisconsin Income Tax (full-year residents).
  * **Form 1NPR:** Nonresident and Part-Year Resident Income Tax.
* **Corporations:**
  * **Form 4:** Wisconsin Non-Combined Corporation Franchise or Income Tax Return.
  * **Form 6:** Combined Corporation Franchise or Income Tax Return (for unitary groups).
* **Pass-Through Entities:**
  * **Form 3:** Wisconsin Partnership Return (includes Schedule 3-ET for electing partnerships).
  * **Form 5S:** Wisconsin Tax-Option (S) Corporation Franchise or Income Tax Return (includes Schedule 5S-ET for electing S corporations).
  * **Form PW-1:** Wisconsin Nonresident Income or Franchise Tax Withholding on Pass-Through Entity Income.
  * **Forms 1CNS / 1CNP:** Composite returns for nonresident S corporation shareholders and partners, respectively.
* *Applicability:* Tax years 2025 and 2026.
* **Official URLs:**
  * https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/Form/2025-Individual.aspx
  * https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/Form/2025-Corporation.aspx
  * https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/Form/2025-Pass-Through.aspx
